In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the political conditions to foster an effective recognition and use of OER between higher education institutions are not yet fully developed.

(1) the political conditions for an effective exchange of Open Educational Resources (and more in general for an effective exchange between Higher Education Institutions) are not yet in place, and that there is a need for a change at both national and EU levels; (2) a change is needed to ensure a better and more effective recognition of the work carried out by teachers, and to ensure a more effective exchange between Higher education institutions, in particular through the exchange of OER.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the exchange of OER in HEIs is a complex and multifaceted process, and that the creation of political conditions for effective exchange of OEr is a process that requires a lot of effort, but is also a rewarding process.

OER are a great opportunity for Higher Education Institutions to improve the quality and the effectiveness of the learning process, but the political conditions must be created for an effective exchange of these resources.

the recognition of OER as valid educational materials in Higher Education Institutions is a necessary condition for their exchange between HEIs.
